messages:
maria: heads-up — we're getting a customer escalation: sustained p99 spikes on text-generation in eu-west (customer: AcmeMaps). Support saw the surge starting ~09:12 UTC and it's still noisy. API errors are low, but tails have ballooned.

jordan: any initial traces? is it a model/infra regression or workload shift?

oliver: I pulled traces — bucketed by request id. p50/p90 OK, p95 and p99 jump around when prefix cache miss rate > ~20%. Looks correlated to KV/prefix cache evictions.

sara: repro steps from support: run same prompt set against hosted/redwood-dense-1, single-tenant route. They saw 250ms -> 1.2s p99. We have logs: prefix_cache.miss_rate spiking to 0.35.

maria: tagging @vincent to check recent runtime changes — any cache key normalization work merged in last 24h?

vincent: I merged a PR that canonicalizes keys to lowercase for one path (opt) but I scoped it. Not across all callers. I did change eviction hint scoring slightly (LRU bias -> size-aware). Could be related.

oliver: logs show a lot of near-duplicate keys differing in trailing space or "\u00A0" non-breaking spaces. Example log:
```
[2026-03-15T09:13:02Z] route=redwood-dense-1 req=abc123 prefix_key="/user/123/profile " cache_hit=false
[2026-03-15T09:13:02Z] route=redwood-dense-1 req=def456 prefix_key="/user/123/profile" cache_hit=false
```
That's causing effective cache fragmentation — lots of hot logical prefixes mapped to different keys => thrash.

jordan: so two contributors: key normalization bug and eviction policy change that punishes small entries? both can amplify miss rate.

maria: mitigation plan? support asked for quick mitigation (customer downtime unacceptable).

oliver: immediate mitigations (quick):
- roll back the eviction-policy change to previous LRU bias (safe and quick).
- add a hotfix that normalizes prefix keys (strip trailing whitespace + unicode normalize) in the prefix hashing path (can be toggled by feature flag).
- warm the cache for known hot prefixes from metrics (preload top-200 prefixes).

sara: support can throttle the customer's traffic to reduce thrash while we fix — they prefer not to throttle but will if needed. Also can enable temporary route-level pinning to a dedicated cache shard.

vincent: I can cut a rollback PR for the eviction change now. Also will push a feature-flagged key-normalizer to runtime, with a kill switch. Should be deployable in ~20m if CI green.

maria: good. oliver, can you create a warmup job list? get top prefixes (by qps last 10m) and pre-insert them into cache. That will reduce cold misses while we deploy.

oliver: on it. extracting top prefixes now: generating a preload payload. Will post the command and sample in a sec.

oliver: preload script snippet:
```
# list top prefixes
curl -sS "https://metrics.internal/api/top_prefixes?route=redwood-dense-1&minutes=10" | jq -r '.prefixes[]' > /tmp/top_prefixes.txt
# preload
cat /tmp/top_prefixes.txt | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -X POST "https://runtime.internal/cache/preload" -d '{"prefix":"{}"}'
```

maria: also create an alert to page if prefix_cache.miss_rate > 0.25 for 5m (p95 regression threshold). We need a runbook entry. Support-ops, can you draft a short customer-facing note?

support-ops: drafting now. Will tell AcmeMaps: investigating latency spikes, applied immediate mitigations (cache warmup + rollback of recent eviction change), next update in 30m.

jordan: postmortem TODOs (capture after incident):
- root cause: cache key fragmentation (edge whitespace/unicode) + eviction policy change that increased churn.
- why it hit p95/p99 but not p50: hot prefixes are very heavy skewed.
- detection: missing alert on prefix miss rate; we had only overall cache hit alert.
- remediation: durable fix for key normalization library, add canonicalizer at callsites, tighten unit tests for unicode/whitespace, add telemetry for per-prefix keys cardinality, revert eviction scoring tweak, and consider switching to LFU or seg-LRU for prefix caches.

vincent: agree. I also want to add identity-testing: fuzz a batch of keys with random unicode whitespace to ensure normalized outputs stable.

maria: timeline: rollback PR -> deploy (canary) -> enable key-normalizer feature flag -> run warmup -> monitor for 30m -> if stable, flip flag globally -> close customer loop.

oliver: after warmup and enabling normalize flag in canary, initial numbers look promising: prefix_cache.miss_rate dropped 0.34 -> 0.06 on canary nodes; p99 on canary reduced from 1.2s -> 380ms.

support-ops: AcmeMaps updated: appreciates quick action, asked for postmortem and SLA credit if not solved within 24h.

maria: keep this thread updated. if rollback or flag flip triggers regressions, rollback and escalate. Also add a note to eng-runtime/postmortems with timeline.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-eviction-2026-03-15 to canary cluster (canary-3) by vincent — CI passed, deploying... :rocket:

vincent: canary deployed. monitoring now.

oliver: metrics holding steady at 09:50 UTC — miss_rate ~0.05, p99 ~360ms on canary. I'll promote to 50% then 100% if green.

maria: thanks everyone. after close, write a short blameless postmortem and schedule a follow-up to decide long-term eviction policy and add a per-prefix cardinality alert.

sara: adding runbook link: https://playbook.internal/runbooks/prefix-cache-thrash (draft)

support-ops: customer notified at 09:58 UTC — reduced impact visible. will keep monitoring.

maria: marking this thread as in-progress. will update when incident closed. :white_check_mark:
